title: Clinical AI conversation transcript (import format), draft 0.2 (legacy 0.1 records supported)
description: One conversation per JSON object, one object per line in a .jsonl file. Text is the only content field; everything else is provenance, de-identification state, and annotations. A record whose deidentification.status is not one of the allowed values is invalid and the importer refuses it; the value 'identified' is deliberately absent from the enum so that identified material can never validate. Version contract: a record labelled schema_version 0.1 is a legacy record and validates exactly as before, and it must not carry any 0.2-only field (turns[].tool_calls, turns[].tool_call_id, provenance.run_manifest); those fields require schema_version 0.2. The if/then block at the top level enforces the forward labelling.

schema_version.description: 0.2 (proposed 2026-09-16) adds optional, harness-agnostic fields: turns[].tool_calls and turns[].tool_call_id, which record the assistant's tool calls and pair each tool turn with its call, and provenance.run_manifest, a digest reference to the closed run manifest of the execution that produced the record. Every 0.1 record validates unchanged under 0.2; a 0.2 record that uses none of the new fields is a 0.1 record.

conversation_id.description: Opaque, stable, and not derived from any identifier of a person (a random id or a hash of the de-identified text). Unique across the input file and the existing transcript store: the importer treats a repeat whose whole record (everything but provenance.import_utc and importer_sha) is identical as an idempotent duplicate (skipped, reported); a repeat with the same turns but different metadata or annotations as a metadata conflict (refused, to be merged by hand); and a repeat with different turns as a conflict (refused).

system.description: The deploying organisation's label for the assistant, e.g. a product or pilot name. Never a person.

model.description: Model as configured, if known. Required for counterfactual eligibility (docs/framework_design.md section 3.1): a record with a null model is imported for the observational path only.

model_version.description: Exact version string the provider returned, if the capture had it.

captured_utc.description: ISO 8601 UTC instant. The pattern checks shape only; the importer also parses it and refuses an impossible date or time (section 3.3).

method.description: Tool or procedure used; null only for synthetic.

reviewed_by.description: Role of the human who confirmed the de-identification (a role, not a name); null only for synthetic.

deidentification.description: De-identification state. When status is 'deidentified', method, reviewed_by and reviewed_utc must be non-null (the audit evidence the privacy gate promises); they may be null only for 'synthetic'.

basis.description: Legal or ethical basis for research use (e.g. an IRB determination reference), as a label.

user_is.description: Who the human turns come from. The study's contrast is between patient-framed and clinician-framed wording of the same situation; this field records which the conversation is, so paired analysis can match across conversations.

text.description: The turn's text. For a tool turn, the tool result string exactly as the model received it.

attachments_omitted.description: Count of non-text items dropped at import (images, files). Required on every turn, an explicit 0 when nothing was omitted, so a dropped attachment is always reported and never silently lost. A user turn with a positive count is ineligible for the counterfactual step (its situation cannot be reproduced from text), and an assistant turn with a positive count is judged as an incomplete reply, both reported by name (section 3.3).

reply_to.description: For an assistant turn: the turn_id of the user turn it answers. Optional; when absent the importer pairs the assistant turn with the immediately preceding turn only if that turn is a user turn (docs/framework_design.md section 3.3), and an assistant turn that cannot be paired unambiguously is ineligible for the counterfactual step (unpaired_reply).

call_id.description: The call identifier the harness assigned; the tool turn that answers it carries the same value in tool_call_id.

arguments.description: The parsed arguments as the model emitted them, an open object because its shape is the tool's; unparseable arguments leave this empty and set parse_error. Part of the turns array, so provenance.text_sha256 covers it.

parse_error.description: The harness's parse error text when the model's call could not be parsed; null otherwise. Recorded, never dropped: a malformed call is target behaviour.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls the assistant made in this turn, in emission order; present only on assistant turns. Target behaviour, not an analysis sidecar.

tool_call_id.description: On a tool turn: the call_id this result answers, which must name a tool call on an earlier assistant turn of the record (import-time check). Null or absent on every other role.

topic.description: Coarse topic label from the study's specialty map, if assigned.

value.description: One of that dimension's declared values, or the reserved `not_applicable`, whose meaning is defined per dimension by the registry entry and its prompt file: it is reserved for the case where the object or context the dimension requires is genuinely unavailable (recorded as unavailable and counted; no contrast is generated). Absence of a behaviour uses that dimension's declared substantive absence value when one exists, never not_applicable.

annotator.description: Non-empty, and shaped by `method` (checked at import, section 3.3): for rule, `rule:<name>:<version>`; for judge, `judge:<model_version>:<prompt sha256[:12]>` where the digest must equal the current sha256 of the order-preserving canonical form of the dimension's judge_prompt_ref file (its own key order, whitespace removed; a stale or fabricated digest is refused); for human, a role label that does not begin with `rule:` or `judge:`, never a name. `method` must be one the dimension enables in `detection.methods`.

rendered_sha256.description: Judge annotations only, refused on any other method (else branch below): sha256 of the fully rendered prompt as sent to the judge, produced by the prompt file's canonical `rendering` algorithm and recomputed at import from that file and the annotated turn's text (section 3.3): a stale, fabricated or differently rendered digest is refused.

framing.description: Per-turn classifications. The schema checks types only; the importer additionally requires (see docs/framework_design.md section 3.3) that turn_id values are unique, that every annotation resolves to exactly one turn with role 'user', and that dimension_id and value are declared in the registry.

importer_sha.description: Git sha of the importer that wrote this record.

text_sha256.description: sha256 (hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical JSON of `turns`: json.dumps(turns, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')), the same canonical form scripts/advice_eval.py uses for its hash chain. A consumer recomputes it and refuses a record whose text changed.

sha256.description: The run manifest's identity digest (its chain.identity_sha256: the manifest with the chain block removed and the record-dependent artifact digests blanked), binding the record to the execution that produced it without a digest cycle.

ref.description: Repo-relative path of that manifest when it is committed; null when only the digest is known.

run_manifest.description: Optional, harness-agnostic reference to a closed run manifest; absent for captures that have none. Execution-specific detail stays in the manifest, never here.
